title: Greece vs Spain: Which Mediterranean Country Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Greece and Spain based on Reddit discussions, real costs, island-hopping logistics, food scenes, and traveler preferences.

faqs.question: Is Greece or Spain cheaper?
faqs.answer: Greece is generally cheaper, though the gap has narrowed. A mid-range budget in Greece runs $80–130/person (mainland/Crete) to $150–180+ on Santorini or Mykonos. Spain runs $90–150/person with Andalusia (Seville, Granada) notably affordable. The Cyclades can be expensive — Mykonos rivals Ibiza for prices. Crete, Rhodes, and smaller islands like Naxos offer much better value. Spain's menu del día lunches ($12–15 including wine) are an unbeatable deal.

faqs.question: Is Greece or Spain better for beaches?
faqs.answer: Greece wins on pure beach quality — the Aegean and Ionian islands offer some of Europe's most stunning beaches. Navagio Beach (Zakynthos), Myrtos (Kefalonia), Elafonisi and Balos Lagoon (Crete) are world-class. Spain's Formentera has some of the clearest Mediterranean water anywhere. For overall beach variety and island hopping culture, Greece; for crystal-clear shallow water, Formentera (Spain).

faqs.question: Is Greece or Spain better for food?
faqs.answer: Spain is widely considered to have the superior food scene. San Sebastián has the highest Michelin star density per capita of any city in the world. Regional diversity — Basque pintxos, Valencian paella, Andalusian jamón, Galician seafood — is extraordinary. Greece's food is excellent — fresh, simple, Mediterranean — but less varied and innovative. Greece wins on freshness and ingredients; Spain wins on food culture depth and gastronomy.

faqs.question: Which is better — Greek islands or Spanish islands?
faqs.answer: Greek islands win for island-hopping culture, scenic drama, and variety. Santorini's caldera, Milos's moonscape beaches, Corfu's Venetian old town — the variety is extraordinary. The Spanish Balearics (Mallorca, Menorca, Ibiza, Formentera) are beautiful but more developed. For pure island-hopping adventure, Greece. For beach club nightlife, Ibiza. For the clearest water in Europe, Formentera.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Greece vs Spain?
faqs.answer: Both are best April–June and September–October. These shoulder months offer warm weather, manageable crowds, and lower prices. July–August on the Greek islands is very busy and hot. Spain's interior reaches brutal temperatures in July–August (38–42°C). The ideal: May for wildflowers in both countries, September for warm weather with far fewer tourists. April in Seville during Feria de Abril is a legendary Spanish experience.

faqs.question: Can you combine Greece and Spain in one trip?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it makes a superb 2–3 week itinerary. Fly into Barcelona, spend 3–4 days, fly to Athens (2.5hr direct, $50–150), spend 2–3 days in Athens, island-hop for 5–7 days. Alternatively: Madrid → Seville (AVE 2.5hr) → fly Athens → island-hop → home. Greece and Spain are roughly 2,000km apart — flying is the only connection option, typically via another European hub if no direct service available.

faqs.question: Which country has better nightlife — Greece or Spain?
faqs.answer: Spain wins on nightlife culture — dinner at 10pm is normal, clubs open at 2am, the night doesn't end until 8am in Madrid. Barcelona's nightlife rivals Berlin. Ibiza is globally famous for superclub culture. Greece has excellent summer nightlife — Mykonos is legendary in July–August, Athens' Gazi and Psiri bar scenes are vibrant — but Spain's nightlife is more deeply embedded in everyday cultural life, year-round.

sectionVerdicts.why: Spain wins on food culture, diversity, and gastronomy. Greece wins on simplicity and freshness — the best Greek meals have a purity that's hard to match. For serious food travelers, Spain is a pilgrimage; for Mediterranean simplicity at its finest, Greece.
sectionVerdicts.whoThisMattersFor: Matters most if food quality, variety, or meal budgets will shape your trip between  and .

sectionVerdicts.why: Greece wins on island-hopping variety, ancient character, and the unique geology of the Cyclades. The Santorini caldera and Milos moonscape beaches have no Spanish equivalent. Spain's Formentera wins for pure water clarity. For island culture and variety, Greece; for crystal-clear Mediterranean water, Formentera.
sectionVerdicts.whoThisMattersFor: Matters most if this category is one of your top trip-deciding factors.

sectionVerdicts.why: Comparable costs outside the premium Greek islands. If Santorini or Mykonos are on your list, budget significantly more than Spain equivalents. For budget travelers: mainland Greece and Crete vs. Andalusia in Spain are similar prices with different character.
sectionVerdicts.whoThisMattersFor: Matters most if nightly rates, meal prices, or transport costs will change how long you can stay.

sectionVerdicts.why: Spain's transport network is dramatically better for mainland travel. Greece requires more planning for island-hopping — you're dependent on ferry schedules and weather. Both countries reward having a rental car for rural exploration.
sectionVerdicts.whoThisMattersFor: Matters most if you care about ease, transfer friction, and how much time you lose moving between sights.

sectionVerdicts.why: May–June and September are the sweet spots for both countries. April is excellent for Spain (Easter celebrations in Seville are extraordinary). October is excellent for Greece (islands still warm, far fewer tourists). Both countries are best avoided in peak August crowds.
sectionVerdicts.whoThisMattersFor: Matters most if seasonality, rain, heat, or crowd levels could make or break the trip.

sectionVerdicts.why: Both countries have exceptional accommodation at every price point. Santorini is the most expensive Greek option; San Sebastián is priciest in Spain. Andalusia (Granada, Seville) and Greek mainland / Crete are the best value areas in each country.
sectionVerdicts.whoThisMattersFor: Matters most if neighborhood choice, hotel value, or day-trip convenience is a big part of the decision.

sectionVerdicts.why: Greece wins on ancient history — the Acropolis, Delphi, and Olympia are unparalleled. Spain wins on architectural variety — from Moorish Alhambra to modernist Gaudí, the span is extraordinary. History lovers need both.
sectionVerdicts.whoThisMattersFor: Matters most if you are choosing based on atmosphere, heritage, and what kind of experience feels more memorable.
